review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read Mathlib's ProjectiveSpectrum/Functor.lean, where `comapFun` is `@[simps]` and `map_id` is a theorem. I read the downstream users in SymmetricAlgebraProj.lean and examples/TransportExamples.lean. The two existing @[simp] `_apply` lemmas are rfl lemmas whose right-hand sides are in terms of `comapFun`, so I found no loop or competing rule. The findings are about missing simp lemmas, not wrong ones. I did not run Lean, so I can't say whether the proposed lemmas would fire. In particular, the `Homeomorph` coercion form in the `_apply` lemma would need a check. I did not flag `map_toSpecZero`, which is not simp. Its right-hand side is a composite of morphisms with no obvious canonical form, and I saw no use that needs it.

findings.problem: The equivalence and the closed-points equivalence get @[simp] apply lemmas, but the homeomorph built from them gets none (neither a coercion lemma nor a `toEquiv` lemma). An application `⇑(projectiveSpectrumHomeomorphOfInverseGradedRingHom f g hfg hgf) x` therefore stays stuck under `simp`, because a structure-instance `def` is not unfolded by the simplifier. The file already works around this. `projClosedPointsEquivOfInverseGradedRingHom` has to use a manual `change IsClosed ({x} ...) ↔ IsClosed ({projectiveSpectrumHomeomorphOfInverseGradedRingHom f g hfg hgf x} ...)` before it can use `Set.image_singleton` and `isClosed_image`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem projectiveSpectrumHomeomorphOfInverseGradedRingHom_apply (f g hfg hgf) (p : ProjectiveSpectrum ℬ) : projectiveSpectrumHomeomorphOfInverseGradedRingHom f g hfg hgf p = ProjectiveSpectrum.comapFun f (irrelevant_le_map_of_comp_eq_id f g hfg) p := rfl`. Optionally add a `toEquiv` rfl lemma as well. Alternatively, mark the definition `@[simps! apply]` or `@[simps! toEquiv]`, if that is compatible with the explicit proof fields.
findings.benefit: `simp` can then reduce homeomorph applications to the explicit `comapFun` form already used for the equivalence. The `change` in the closed-points definition can become plain simp rewriting. Users who go through the homeomorph, for example via `RootClient.lean`, no longer have to unfold by hand.

findings.problem: Only the forward direction is covered by a simp lemma. The `invFun` direction is `comapFun g ...`, but there is no `symm_apply` lemma. An expression `(projectiveSpectrumEquivOfInverseGradedRingHom f g hfg hgf).symm p` is stuck, because `Equiv.symm_apply_apply` only fires on a composite. The same gap applies to `projClosedPointsEquivOfInverseGradedRingHom` and `closedPointsEquivOfIso`, where `.symm` has no description either. The in-repo example `transport_point_roundtrip` proves its round trip by invoking `.left_inv p` directly, and `transported_closed_point_underlying` needs `simpa only using`. That suggests the simp set does not give a usable interface for these statements.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` rfl lemmas `projectiveSpectrumEquivOfInverseGradedRingHom_symm_apply : (projectiveSpectrumEquivOfInverseGradedRingHom f g hfg hgf).symm p = ProjectiveSpectrum.comapFun g (irrelevant_le_map_of_comp_eq_id g f hgf) p`. Add the analogous `projClosedPointsEquivOfInverseGradedRingHom_symm_apply_coe`. For `closedPointsEquivOfIso`, add `((closedPointsEquivOfIso e).symm y : Y.. ) = e.inv y`, with the stated type adjusted to the file's carrier types. Alternatively, use `@[simps]` on the definitions, if that is compatible with the explicit fields.
findings.benefit: Terms such as `(equiv).symm (equiv p)` and closed-point inverses then normalise to explicit `comapFun` or `e.inv` forms. `Equiv.symm_apply_apply` can also be applied after those forms are reached. The roundtrip statement in the examples would not need `left_inv`, and downstream users get the same coverage for both directions.
